source: MSTA's answer key (printed in the paper)

answers.value: Mass, length, time, temperature (Y, W, U, V)
answers.reasoning: Fundamental quantities do not depend on other quantities. Mass, length, time and temperature are fundamental. Weight (mass times g) and momentum (mass times velocity) are derived, so every option with X or Z is wrong.

1 is true: a charged object attracts a neutral one by induction. 2 is false: gaining electrons makes an atom negative. 3 is true: charge is never created, only transferred from one body to another. 4 is true: losing electrons leaves an atom positive.

answers.runnerUp: B, if the setup is read as measuring the block's acceleration to test Newton's second law
answers.reasoning: When enough load is hung, the pull of the thread (a force) moves the block along the table, and the scale beside the block measures how far it moves (the displacement). Knowing the force and the displacement lets us verify that work done is \(W = Fs\).

Pressure is force divided by area, \(P = \frac{F}{A}\). The weight is the same in every position, so pressure is least when the area touching the ground is largest, which happens when the person lies on the back.
Work, energy and heat are all forms of energy and are measured in joules. Specific heat is measured in J/kg°C (joule per kilogram per degree), not in joules.

answers.value: Density of liquid and volume of the object (1, 2)
answers.reasoning: Buoyant force equals the weight of liquid displaced: \(F = V\rho g\), where \(V\) is the volume of the object immersed and \(\rho\) is the density of the liquid. The amount of liquid in the vessel, the object's own density and the depth do not change it.
Water freezes at 0 °C. In Fahrenheit that is \(\frac{9}{5}\times 0 + 32 = 32\) °F, and in kelvin it is \(0 + 273 = 273\) K.

answers.value: Volume decreases and pressure decreases (Y, W)
answers.reasoning: Cooling the sealed air makes its molecules move slower, so the pressure of the air falls; the cold metal bottle also contracts slightly. Every other option says the pressure increases, which cannot happen on cooling, so Y and W is the correct choice.

P lies on the bisector, so it makes \(60^\circ\) with each mirror and is \(4\sin 60^\circ = 2\sqrt{3}\) cm from each mirror. Each image is twice that, \(4\sqrt{3}\) cm, from P. The images and P are all 4 cm from the meeting point and \(120^\circ\) apart, so the triangle is equilateral with side \(4\sqrt{3}\) cm and perimeter \(12\sqrt{3}\) cm.

One round is \(2\pi r = 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 70 = 440\) m, so speed is \(\frac{440}{44} = 10\) m/s. He comes back to the starting point, so his displacement is zero and his average velocity is 0 m/s.

answers.value: d = 875 m, v = 35 m/s, a = 2 m/s²
answers.reasoning: From the graph, velocity is 10 m/s at 5 s and 60 m/s at 30 s. Acceleration \(a = \frac{60-10}{30-5} = \frac{50}{25} = 2\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\). Average velocity \(= \frac{10+60}{2} = 35\) m/s, so distance \(= 35\times 25 = 875\) m.

answers.value: P heat energy, Q kinetic energy, R mechanical energy, S electrical energy
answers.reasoning: This is the chain in a steam power plant. The steam in the boiler P carries heat energy; the jet of steam at Q is moving, so it has kinetic energy; it turns the turbine R, giving mechanical energy; and the generator turns that into electrical energy, which reaches the bulb at S. That is option D.
answers.notice: Option (B) can also be defended: the boiler holds compressed steam, and the bulb gives out light. MSTA's key gives (D), the usual chain heat, kinetic, mechanical, electrical. In PYQ Vault mocks this question is awarded to every candidate.

answers.value: Power: g cm² s⁻³ and kg m² s⁻³
answers.reasoning: Power is work per second: \(\mathrm{kg\,m^2 s^{-2}}\) divided by s gives \(\mathrm{kg\,m^2 s^{-3}}\), and in CGS \(\mathrm{g\,cm^2 s^{-3}}\). The force and work options have the wrong power of s, and the units in D belong to force, not pressure.

In parallel every appliance gets the same potential difference (2), so each works at its rated capacity (1), and if one stops working the others still run (4). Statement 3 is false: the current through each appliance depends on its own resistance, so it is not the same.

answers.value: Different wavelengths and different refractive indices
answers.reasoning: White light is made of colours of different wavelengths. Water drops have a different refractive index for each wavelength, so each colour bends by a different amount and the colours spread out into a rainbow.

answers.value: Only the pole (R) is not common
answers.runnerUp: B, if the focal length is treated as different because one piece is concave and another convex (opposite signs)
answers.reasoning: Pieces cut from the same sphere have the same radius of curvature, so the same focal length (half the radius), and their centre of curvature is the centre of that sphere. The pole is the middle point of each mirror's own surface, so it is different for each mirror.
Watt, horse power and N m s⁻¹ (joule per second) are all units of power. \(\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}\) is force per area, a unit of pressure, so it is the odd one out.

answers.value: P = ammeter, Q = key, R = voltmeter, S = resistor
answers.runnerUp: D, which swaps R and S; since R and S are both in the parallel pair, a voltmeter across a resistor is equally correct either way round, so the item may have two right answers
answers.reasoning: P and Q are in the main line with the cell, so they take the ammeter (2) and the key (4), both of which go in series. R and S are joined in parallel, so they take the resistor and the voltmeter, which must be connected across the resistor. S lies on the main wire, so it carries the resistor (1), and R is the loop drawn around it for the voltmeter (3). Options A and C put the voltmeter in series, which is wrong.

In a gas, \(v \propto \sqrt{\frac{T}{M}}\). So 4 is true and 1 is false (speed rises with temperature, it is not inversely proportional). 2 is true. 3 is false: at a fixed temperature, changing the pressure does not change the speed of sound.
The boy is 165 m from wall A and \(495 - 165 = 330\) m from wall B. Echo from A: \(\frac{2\times165}{330} = 1\) s. Echo from B: \(\frac{2\times330}{330} = 2\) s. The difference is \(2 - 1 = 1\) s.
When the kinetic energy becomes half, 490 J has turned into potential energy. \(mgh = 490\), so \(h = \frac{490}{2\times 9.8} = 25\) m.
\(p = mv\) is constant, so \(v = \frac{p}{m}\): velocity is inversely proportional to mass. The graph is a curve that falls steeply and then flattens, never touching either axis, which is Figure (A).
Acceleration \(a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{100}{2} = 50\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\). Change in velocity \(= at = 50\times 10 = 500\) m/s.

During free fall the speed increases, so momentum and kinetic energy increase, while the height falls, so potential energy decreases. The mass stays the same, and the total mechanical energy stays constant because potential energy is turned into kinetic energy.

answers.value: All four statements P, Q, R, S are correct
answers.reasoning: Work by the coolie \(= mgh = 80\times 9.8\times 5 = 3920\) J, positive because his force and the motion are both upward (Q, S true). Gravity acts downward against the upward motion, so its work is negative (P true). Power \(= \frac{3920}{4} = 980\) J/s (R true).

answers.value: Copper, aluminium, platinum, nichrome (z, x, y, w)
answers.reasoning: Copper has the lowest resistivity (about \(1.7\times10^{-8}\ \Omega\,m\)), then aluminium (about \(2.7\times10^{-8}\)), then platinum (about \(10.6\times10^{-8}\)). Nichrome, an alloy, is far higher (about \(1.1\times10^{-6}\)).
CD, DVD and pen drive are secondary storage devices that keep data after the power is off. RAM is the computer's primary (main) memory and loses its data when the power is switched off.
Total time \(= 20\times 5 = 100\) h. Power \(= \frac{2.5\ \mathrm{kWh}}{100\ \mathrm{h}} = 0.025\) kW \(= 25\) W.

answers.value: Image is virtual and magnified (X, W)
answers.reasoning: A concave mirror gives an erect image only when the object is between the pole and the focus. That image is virtual (X true), so it cannot be taken on a screen (Y false), and it is enlarged, so the magnification is more than +1 (W true, Z false).

answers.runnerUp: A, if the analogy is read as recovering pure water from muddy water by distillation
answers.reasoning: Kerosene and water do not mix, so they are separated by a physical method (a separating funnel). Muddy water has fine insoluble clay particles suspended in it, and these are separated by spinning the mixture fast, which is centrifugation. Distillation and chromatography are used for dissolved substances.

answers.value: Lime, silica, alumina, iron oxide, gypsum
answers.runnerUp: C, if magnesia is counted as a listed ingredient instead of gypsum
answers.reasoning: Portland cement is made by heating lime and clay (which supplies silica, alumina and iron oxide), and gypsum is added to the clinker to slow down setting. So its ingredients are lime, silica, alumina, iron oxide and gypsum. Option A lists concrete, not cement.
Hematite, limonite and siderite are ores of iron. Bauxite is the ore of aluminium, so it is the odd one out.
A low-pressure sodium vapour lamp contains sodium with a small amount of neon and argon gas. These gases start the discharge and warm the lamp until the sodium vaporises.

answers.value: Potassium ferrocyanide, platinum nitrate, chlorophyll, vitamin B-12
answers.runnerUp: D, if 'complex compounds' is read as large biological molecules rather than metal complexes
answers.reasoning: A complex compound has a metal atom bonded to a group of surrounding atoms or ions. Potassium ferrocyanide has iron, chlorophyll has magnesium and vitamin B-12 has cobalt at its centre. Common salt, urea, carbohydrates and proteins are not metal complexes, so every other option contains a wrong member.
Galvanizing (zinc coating), tinning (tin coating), anodizing (a protective oxide layer on aluminium) and alloying (as in stainless steel) all protect metals from corrosion.

Magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) is a mild base that neutralises extra acid in the stomach, so it is used as an antacid. Potassium hydroxide and calcium hydroxide are too strong and harmful to swallow.

I is right: an acid reacts with a base (sodium bicarbonate) to form a salt, a neutralization reaction. II is right: citrate is \(\mathrm{C_6H_5O_7^{3-}}\), so sodium citrate is \(\mathrm{Na_3C_6H_5O_7}\). III is wrong: sodium citrate dissolves in water. IV is right: sodium bicarbonate is sodium hydrogen carbonate.

answers.runnerUp: A, if copper oxide's blue colour is taken as the bluish green
answers.reasoning: Iron(II) oxide (ferrous oxide) gives glass a bluish green colour, as seen in many bottles. Copper oxide gives a peacock blue colour, while calcium oxide adds no colour.
In \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), carbon is 12 and oxygen is \(2\times16 = 32\), so the ratio is \(12:32 = 3:8\). Sulphur dioxide is \(32:32 = 1:1\) and magnesium oxide is \(24:16 = 3:2\).

Molecular masses: \(\mathrm{H_2O} = 18\), \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 23+16+1 = 40\), \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 12+32 = 44\), \(\mathrm{MgCl_2} = 24+71 = 95\). In ascending order: \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), NaOH, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\).
Sodium phosphate is \(\mathrm{Na_3PO_4}\). Sodium forms \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) and the phosphate radical carries a charge of 3 minus, \(\mathrm{PO_4^{3-}}\), which is why three sodium ions are needed.

Carbon dioxide turns to gas at about \(-78\) °C, oxygen boils at about \(-183\) °C, argon at about \(-186\) °C and nitrogen at about \(-196\) °C. From highest to lowest: \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), \(\mathrm{O_2}\), Ar, \(\mathrm{N_2}\).
Bromine has atomic number 35, so a neutral atom has 35 electrons. The \(\mathrm{Br^-}\) ion has gained one electron, giving 36.

answers.value: (NH₄)₂SO₄, basic radical NH₄⁺, acidic salt, fertilizer
answers.reasoning: Ammonium is \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\) and sulphate is \(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}\), so the formula is \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}\) and the basic radical is \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\). It comes from a strong acid and a weak base, so it is an acidic salt, and it is used as a nitrogen fertilizer for soil.
Sulphuric acid, sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide dissociate almost completely in water (strong). Formic acid, HCOOH, dissociates only partly, so it is a weak acid and the odd one out.
Molar mass of NaOH \(= 23+16+1 = 40\) g/mol, so 60 g is \(\frac{60}{40} = 1.5\) mol. Molarity \(= \frac{1.5\ \mathrm{mol}}{2\ \mathrm{L}} = 0.75\) M.

answers.value: Sulphamic acid, boric acid, oxalic acid (II, III, V)
answers.reasoning: Sulphamic acid, boric acid and oxalic acid are crystalline solids at room temperature. Carbonic acid exists only in solution (carbon dioxide in water), and hydrochloric acid is a solution of hydrogen chloride gas.

I is true: each side has 1 Ca, 2 N, 8 O and 4 H, so the equation is balanced. II is false: \(\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2}\) comes from a strong acid and a strong base, so it is a neutral salt. III is true: a neutral salt solution has pH 7. IV is not right as stated: \(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}\) is slaked lime, while lime (quicklime) is CaO.
Sulphur (rhombic, monoclinic), phosphorus (white, red) and carbon (diamond, graphite) all show allotropy. Chlorine does not have allotropes, so it is the odd one out.

Smithsonite is the ore of zinc carbonate, \(\mathrm{ZnCO_3}\). In the same way, calcite is the mineral form of calcium carbonate, \(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\). Calamine is also a zinc ore, cryolite is \(\mathrm{Na_3AlF_6}\) and carnallite is a potassium magnesium chloride.

I is true: \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is heavier than air. II is false: coal powder does not dissolve in kerosene. III is false: about 0.03% \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is in the air we breathe in; exhaled air has about 4%. IV is true: liquid methane is much lighter than water. So the statements that are not false are I and IV.

Sodium bicarbonate reacts with sulphuric acid: \(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O + 2CO_2}\), so P is \(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3}\) and Q is \(\mathrm{2H_2O}\). Calcium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid: \(\mathrm{CaCO_3 + 2HCl \rightarrow CaCl_2 + H_2O + CO_2}\), so R is 2HCl and S is \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\).

Methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\), has only one carbon atom in each molecule, the smallest possible hydrocarbon chain. Fewer carbon atoms for the hydrogen present means less \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is formed for the energy released. Being a gas, colourless or inflammable has nothing to do with the amount of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\).
Sea water is mostly sodium chloride, so chlorine and sodium are the most plentiful. Magnesium salts come next, and potassium salts are present in the smallest amount of these four.
Betanin comes from beetroot, anthocyanin from purple and red fruits and flowers, and beta-carotene from carrots, so all three are natural colours. Indigo carmine is a synthetic food dye.

answers.value: The wrong pair is HID lamp and krypton-82
answers.reasoning: Phosphorus-32 is used to treat polycythemia and radium-223 to treat cancer that has spread to bone, so those pairs are right. High intensity discharge (HID) lamps use krypton-85, not krypton-82, so pair D is wrong. Note that pair C is not right either: cobalt-60 is used to treat cancer, while tumours are usually detected with other isotopes such as arsenic-74.
answers.notice: Two pairs are wrong as printed: (D), since HID lamps use krypton-85, and (C), since cobalt-60 treats cancer rather than detecting tumours. MSTA's key gives (D). In PYQ Vault mocks this question is awarded to every candidate.

answers.reasoning: Each alpha particle removes mass 4 and atomic number 2. Two alphas from A (214, 90) give B with mass \(214 - 8 = 206\) and atomic number \(90 - 4 = 86\). Each beta particle leaves the mass unchanged and raises the atomic number by 1, so three betas give C with mass 206 and atomic number \(86 + 3 = 89\).

answers.value: P soft water, Q hard water, R sodium chloride, S zeolite
answers.runnerUp: C, if the side tap P is taken as the sodium chloride inlet and the top pipes as the water inlet and outlet
answers.reasoning: In the figure, Q has an arrow going into a pipe that reaches the bottom, so hard water enters at Q and rises (upward arrows) through the bed S, which is the zeolite (permutit). The softened water is drawn off from the side tap P. R at the top is used to send in sodium chloride solution to regenerate the zeolite.
Epsom salt is magnesium sulphate heptahydrate, \(\mathrm{MgSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}\), so each unit holds 7 water molecules.

1 is true: the cactus stem stores water and food and carries out photosynthesis. 4 is true: the stem is green and fleshy. 3 is false: leaves are reduced to spines so very little water is lost. Statement 2 is not offered with 1 and 4, so the answer is 1 and 4.

answers.runnerUp: A, if fumigation of the stored grain is meant rather than spraying the bags
answers.reasoning: Malathion is the insecticide sprayed on gunny bags of stored grain to keep insects away. Aluminium phosphide is a fumigant tablet placed among grains, not a spray, and nitrite and sodium benzoate are food preservatives.

Pancreatic juice contains enzymes such as trypsin, lipase and amylase. Bile is made by the liver, and mucus is secreted by the walls of the stomach and intestine, so 1 and 4 are not from the pancreas.
Inorganic ions in plasma such as sodium, potassium and calcium control the working of muscles and nerves. Albumin keeps water balance, and prothrombin and fibrinogen help blood to clot.

answers.runnerUp: D, if the tiltmeter is singled out as the one that measures angle rather than length
answers.reasoning: All four instruments watch the Earth's crust. A seismometer records the shaking (seismic waves) of an earthquake, while a creepmeter, strainmeter and tiltmeter measure slow movement and deformation of the ground, so the seismometer is the odd one.

answers.value: P inner membrane, Q outer membrane, R matrix, S cristae
answers.reasoning: In the figure Q points to the smooth outermost covering, the outer membrane. P points to the membrane just inside it, the inner membrane. S points to the folds of the inner membrane, the cristae, and R points to the dotted fluid filling the inside, the matrix.

answers.runnerUp: C, if lignin is taken as the main polymer added as per requirement and pectin is counted with it
answers.reasoning: Every plant cell wall is made of cellulose and pectin. Other polymers such as lignin, suberin and cutin are added to the wall only where the plant needs them, for strength or to stop water loss. Only option D has two such polymers and no cellulose or pectin.

U is wrong: green colour is due to chlorophyll. V is wrong: carotene is orange-yellow, not blue. W is right: xanthophyll is yellow. X is right: anthocyanin gives purple colour. Y is wrong: carotene does not give dark pink. Z is right too, but the only option made of correct pairs alone is X and W.

answers.value: Cellular (internal) respiration: glucose slowly burnt in cells
answers.reasoning: The equation shows glucose being oxidised with oxygen to give carbon dioxide, water and energy. This happens inside cells, where dissolved nutrients like glucose are slowly burnt. Breathing in air, exchange of gases and transport of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) are other stages of respiration.
The trunk of a banana plant is a false stem (pseudostem) made of tightly rolled leaf bases. The real stem is underground.

answers.runnerUp: B, if the setter means that hyphae go into the material only for food and not to reproduce
answers.reasoning: Fungal spores float in the air, hyphae go deep into the material they grow on, and fungi spoil wooden items, so A, B and D describe fungi. The usual school account says fungi multiply by spores, so C is meant as the odd statement. Strictly, many fungi do also reproduce sexually, which makes this item weak.
answers.notice: As printed every statement is true of fungi: many fungi do reproduce sexually, as well as by spores. MSTA's key gives (C). In PYQ Vault mocks this question is awarded to every candidate.

answers.value: X metacentric, Y submetacentric, Z acrocentric, W telocentric
answers.reasoning: X has two equal arms with the centromere in the middle, giving a V shape: metacentric. Y has one arm a little longer than the other (L shape): submetacentric. Z has one long and one very short arm (J shape): acrocentric. W has the centromere at its very tip: telocentric.
In sickle-cell anaemia red blood cells break down fast, so the body must make new ones quickly. Folic acid helps in making red blood cells, so patients are advised to take a folic acid tablet daily.
Leber hereditary optic neuropathy is caused by a mutation in the DNA of mitochondria and is passed on only from the mother, so it is a mitochondrial disorder.

In photosynthesis plants take carbon dioxide from the air and turn it into food (biotic carbon). In respiration living things release it back as carbon dioxide. These two processes keep carbon cycling.

answers.value: 1 and 3: grow in moist soil and need water for reproduction
answers.reasoning: Like amphibians, bryophytes live on land but need moist places, and their male gametes need water to swim to the egg. They do not grow in air or in deserts.

answers.runnerUp: C, if the alkaline pancreatic juice is meant
answers.reasoning: The stomach wall secretes hydrochloric acid, which makes food acidic. Bile secreted by the liver makes the food alkaline when it reaches the small intestine, and also breaks fat into small droplets.

Nitrifying bacteria first convert ammonia into nitrite and then nitrite into nitrate; this is nitrification. Ammonification forms ammonia, denitrification returns nitrogen gas to the air, and nitrogen fixation turns nitrogen gas into compounds.

answers.runnerUp: C, if only vaccine production is counted as biotechnology
answers.reasoning: Biotechnology is used to develop improved varieties of cash crops, to grow tissues such as cartilage by tissue culture, and to produce vaccines. So all three are related to biotechnology.

answers.runnerUp: D, if the setter counts acetic acid (vinegar) made from the alcohol as the by-product
answers.reasoning: When the yeast Saccharomyces is added to molasses, it ferments the sugar into ethyl alcohol. Small amounts of esters, which give the smell, form along with it as a by-product. Acetic acid is made later from the alcohol by a different microbe (Acetobacter).
The autonomic nervous system controls involuntary organs such as the heart, lungs and intestines without our will. The central nervous system controls voluntary actions and thinking.
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum, especially in liver cells, makes toxins and drugs water soluble so that they can be flushed out of the body. This is called detoxification.

answers.runnerUp: D, if the question means the places carbon dioxide is found as a gas, air and water
answers.reasoning: Most of the Earth's carbon dioxide is stored in the oceans, where it is dissolved, and in rocks such as limestone, where it is locked up as carbonates. These are the main reservoirs from which it is cycled.

Penicillin acts mainly on one group of bacteria (Gram-positive), so it is a narrow spectrum antibiotic. Ampicillin, amoxicillin and tetracycline act on many kinds of bacteria, so they are broad spectrum.

answers.runnerUp: D, if the setter took these as service areas of the India Meteorological Department
answers.reasoning: The World Meteorological Organization lists food security, water management, transportation and communication among the areas its weather and climate services support. IITM, NOAA and IMD are national bodies.

answers.value: 1 and 2: cup-like shape and thin wall
answers.reasoning: Bowman's capsule is a thin-walled, cup-shaped structure that surrounds the glomerulus and filters blood. Bean shape describes the whole kidney, and it is not thick or muscular.
The hypothalamus in the brain controls the pituitary gland by sending it hormones, and the pituitary in turn controls the other glands.

In the Venn diagram P lies only in the DNA circle and T only in the RNA circle; the shared middle part holds adenine, guanine and cytosine. Thymine is found only in DNA and uracil only in RNA, so P is thymine and T is uracil.

answers.runnerUp: A, if Cochin is counted as a dual-purpose rather than a meat breed
answers.reasoning: Black Rock is a dual-purpose breed kept for both eggs and meat. Ancona and Leghorn are egg-laying breeds, and Cochin is mainly a heavy meat breed.

answers.runnerUp: A, if first aid for a fracture is meant, though a fracture needs splinting first
answers.reasoning: RICE stands for Rest, Ice, Compression and Elevation. It is the first aid for soft tissue injuries such as a contusion (bruise) or sprain, reducing swelling and pain. Heatstroke and epilepsy need different care, and a fracture must first be kept still with a splint.

answers.runnerUp: C, if a later European discovery was meant
answers.reasoning: NASA's planet-hunting telescope TESS found GJ 357 d, announced as the first nearby super-Earth that may be able to support life.
Zydus Cadila launched Remdac, the cheapest Indian brand of the COVID-19 drug remdesivir, in 2020.
SLV-3 (Satellite Launch Vehicle 3) was India's first indigenous launch vehicle; it placed the Rohini satellite in orbit in 1980. ASLV, PSLV and GSLV came later.

answers.runnerUp: A, if the carbon dioxide released by soil microbes and roots is meant
answers.reasoning: Radon is a radioactive gas given off naturally from uranium in soil and rocks. Ozone and formaldehyde are not released by soil.
MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) uses a strong magnetic field, radio waves and a computer to make pictures of the body. It does not use X-rays, which is why it is safer than a CT scan.
Europa, Io and Callisto are moons of Jupiter. Titan is the largest moon of Saturn, so any group with Q is wrong.

answers.runnerUp: A, if the setter's source called stomach cancer the silent killer
answers.reasoning: A cancer is called a silent killer when it gives almost no symptoms until it is far advanced. Liver cancer is commonly described this way, since the liver keeps working until much of it is damaged.
An anemometer measures wind speed. A barometer measures air pressure, a hygrometer measures humidity and a radiometer measures radiation.
A giraffe's heart must push blood about two metres up its long neck to the brain, so it has the highest blood pressure of these animals, about twice that of a human.
The colour of a star depends on its surface temperature. The coolest stars look red, medium ones like the Sun yellow, and the hottest stars blue.
